speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pelvic pain, bloating, or difficulty eating due to early satiety? Have you noticed any vaginal bleeding or discharge? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass and significant ascites causing your shortness of breath, I need to assess for signs of metastatic spread. Have you experienced any chest pain, persistent cough, or noticed swelling in your legs? REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CT scan, this presentation of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion (causing shortness of breath) is classic for Meigs syndrome. I need to confirm if the shortness of breath is due to fluid around the lungs. Have you noticed any difficulty breathing when lying flat, or any swelling in your legs? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The triad of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with a normal CT scan strongly suggests Meigs syndrome, likely due to an ovarian fibroma. To confirm the benign nature of the mass and rule out malignancy, I will request a tumor marker test. REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a solid ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with normal CA-125 and no evidence of metastasis is diagnostic for Meigs syndrome, likely caused by an ovarian fibroma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
